method.label: Shift and subtract the repeating block

annotationRationale: Base-k place value turns a two-place shift into multiplication by k squared. Cancelling the repeated tail produces a quadratic solved by factoring.
sourceMethod: Followed the official shift-and-subtract alternative, explaining the base-k value of the integer block 23 and enforcing the admissible-base restriction.

review.mathCheck: The repeating fraction equals (2k+3)/(k^2-1). Equating this to 7/51 gives (k-16)(7k+10)=0. Only k=16 satisfies the integer-base requirement k≥4, confirming choice D.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded expansion of official #18's shift-and-subtract alternative on p.11, followed by the factorization on p.10. The geometric-series approach is not required.
review.annotationCheck: The two-place shift, value of the digit block, cancellation, factorization, and rejection of the inadmissible root are explained sufficiently for AMC 12.
